crseAttrs.descrformal: AG-Other Physical and Life Sciences Requirement

classes.description: Focuses on helping individuals understand how scientific information relates to the issues they face as citizens, in management decision making, and in public policy. To what extent should genetic engineering of crop plants be permitted? Should we place limits on fossil fuel consumption as a means of limiting global warming and global climate change? Must human endeavors be restricted in certain areas to maintain diversity? The format of this course is interactive, with lectures and discussions about how we as a society deal with controversial issues. This course is suitable for life sciences majors.
catalogOutcomes: Explain, evaluate, and effectively interpret basic concepts in cell and molecular biology.
Explain, evaluate, and effectively interpret basic concepts in general ecology and biodiversity.
Integrate qualitative information to reach defensible and creative conclusions about the impacts of climate change, genetic engineering, and biodiversity on the natural world and society.
Communicate effectively through writing, speech, and visual information via written exams, writing assignments and class discussion concerning the above topics.
Articulate the views of people with diverse perspectives on the above issues.

classes.subject: PLSCI
classes.description: Ecuador is one of the most biodiverse and climatically varied countries in the world. This course explores evolutionary ecology across a spectacular altitudinal gradient from the high latitudes paramo of the Andes into the highly biodiverse lowland tropical rainforest. The course begins with a cohort building retreat with workshops on field safety and cultural humility. Then, through field-based lectures and workshops, data collection, self-driven reflections, we explore the vast differences in the ecology and evolution across these biomes. The course concludes with an intendent research project at the Tiputini Biological Station one of the most biodiverse places on earth comprising a canopy of enormous tropical trees covered by fascinating epiphytes and lianas, multiple species of monkeys and tropical birds, and a stunning diversity of arthropods.
classes.catalogEnrollmentPriority: Recommended Prerequisite: A general course in ecology, evolution, biodiversity and/or data analysis (e.g. PLSCI 2430; PLSCI 2015; BIOEE 2233; BIOEE 1780) is recommended but not required.
classes.catalogFee: Field trip, $3,500.  $3500 plus airfare and vaccination.
catalogOutcomes: Make natural history observations and apply them to broader eco-evolutionary theory.
Contrast and quantify ecological and evolutionary differences across different biomes in Ecuador.
Evaluate the role of biotic and abiotic factors in driving ecology and evolution from mountains to tropical forests.
Identify the traits involved in adaptation and how these vary across gradients.
Conduct field research by directly observing natural populations and communities, making inferences with appropriate data science and statistical models.
Reflect on cultural humility associated with visiting remote locations and living within biodiverse communities in a foreign country.

classes.subject: PLSCI
classes.titleLong: Far Beyond Ithaca (FBI): Plant Explorations in Winter

notes.descrlong: This is part two of a multi-semester course. Part two is held January 7, 2027 - January 18, 2027, in Vietnam, with departure from JFK airport on January 6, 2027 and return on January 19, 2027. Enrollment in PLSCI 3401 and participation in winter travel component required to complete PLSCI 3400.

classes.description: In sections of this course, students travel with faculty to a domestic or international locale to experience first-hand the issues around a particular challenge in plant sciences, such as climate change and the spread of plant diseases, drought and viticulture, and the tension between biodiversity, species conservation and large-scale agriculture. Students engage with communities, collect and analyze data, and collaborate with peers in a final presentation at the end of the course.
classes.catalogEnrollmentPriority: Enrollment preference given to: Plant Sciences and Agricultural Sciences majors.
classes.catalogFee: Course fee, $5000.  Fees for associated winter trip are approximate and not expected to exceed $5,000 for any one trip. Fee amount varies by class section.
catalogOutcomes: Describe the state of plant communities and/or agroecosystems in the targeted region.
Determine how humans are interfacing with these systems to create challenges or to help mitigate problems.
Explain how events in the targeted region can have impacts at home.
